name: Conductor
title: Ninebrains vs Conductor (conductor.build)
description: Ninebrains vs Conductor, the Mac app for running Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode agents in parallel worktrees: platforms, source, telemetry and checks, sourced.
summary: Mac-native app for parallel agents in worktrees with a pre-merge Checks tab.
answer: Conductor and Ninebrains both run coding agents in parallel, each in its own git worktree. Conductor is a polished Mac app with a pre-merge Checks tab that gathers CI status, review threads and todos. Ninebrains is open source and cross-platform, plans work as a job graph, and blocks completion until configured checks such as tests and a reviewer pass.
note: This page is about conductor.build. Google also has a product called Conductor, a planning and review extension for Gemini CLI; see Ninebrains vs Google Conductor.

what.text: An app that runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode agents in parallel, in isolated workspaces on your Mac.

agents.text: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode.

isolation.text: Git worktrees, which they describe as development isolation, not a security boundary.

verification.text: A Checks tab that collects CI status, PR comments and todos before merge, and may block or discourage merging while required work is open.

telemetry.text: Limited analytics from the app, such as crash logs and which features are used.

chooseThem.text: You are on a Mac and want a polished, native flow from diff to pull request to merge to archive.
You want Cursor and OpenCode agents alongside Claude Code and Codex.
You want one pre-merge view of CI status, review threads and todos.

chooseUs: You are on Windows or Linux, or want the source code under Apache-2.0.
You want work planned as a dependency graph and dispatched to idle lanes.
You want checks to run before work counts as done, not only before merge: tests, screenshots and a read-only reviewer, with retries.
